chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He was asked about a man who bought a garment, and when he cut it, he found flaws in it, and he did not know of that until he cut it. What is the ruling in that case?

He said: 'Accept the garment, or else prepare your companion for satisfaction and reduce a little for him, and it will not harm you, if God wills. If he refuses, then accept the garment, for it is safer for you, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling if a buyer finds a flaw in a garment after cutting it?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of *khiyar al-ayb* (option of defect) is applied to a scenario where the flaw was concealed and discovered post-cutting, highlighting the Shia emphasis on amicable resolution (*sulh*) over rigid litigation. The Imam prioritizes preserving social harmony and mutual consent, suggesting a minor price adjustment as a pragmatic solution before resorting to keeping the item as final settlement. This reflects the broader juristic preference for avoiding unnecessary conflict (*fitna*) and ensuring fairness in commercial transactions.
